brief: One drawer and one spike, both at the very same corner of the same cell, touching.

requirements.requirement: One drawer at a corner of a cell
requirements.evidence: drawer:0#0,0#cut on piece:0,0,0;half-s at q=0,r=0, key n (north cut face, at the corner)

requirements.requirement: One spike at the very same corner of the same cell
requirements.evidence: spike:0#0,0|0,1|1,0 at junction [0,0|0,1|1,0] the north apex of cell 0,0 — same junction that borders the drawer's cell

Both are hosted by piece:0,0,0;half-s — drawer on its north cut and spike at its north corner junction (posMm 47.8,0,82.9). Adjacent pieces at 0,1,0 and 1,0,0 provide the 3-cell cluster required for the spike to exist; meshClash clear.

finish.summary: Placed half-s base at 0,0,0 to expose a north-facing cut for a drawer, clustered two full bases at 0,1,0 and 1,0,0 to create the 3-way junction at the same north corner, then added drawer:0#0,0#cut and spike:0#0,0|0,1|1,0 together at that corner. House rules applied, mesh clear.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
